question: How much of the source backlog is blocked on a corpus that exists, is inventoried with hashes, and is not carried by this release?
answer: Most of it. 99 of the 111 SOURCE_BLOCKED families are in a jurisdiction where the operational Nationwide tree records form-shaped documents this repository does not hold at any hash.
method: Every SHA-256 in data/rcap-all50/nationwide-source-inventory.json cross-mapped against every SHA-256 in data/rcap-all50/local-source-corpus-index.json. Nothing was fetched and nothing was opened: the inventory records hashes and the index records hashes, so this is an arithmetic comparison of two committed records.

theTreeIsNotHere.whyNot: private/source-corpus-environment.txt carries the OFFICIAL_FORMS_SOURCE_DIR export COMMENTED OUT, with the note "A DIFFERENT corpus, not carried by this release. Do not substitute the Master Library for it; the operational-corpus precondition refuses that by name." scripts/rcap-corpus/bootstrap-private-corpus.sh has no acquisition path for it — only that commented export.
theTreeIsNotHere.soThisIsNotExecutableWork: No agent in this container can mount it. Provisioning it is an owner and infrastructure decision, recorded here rather than attempted.

measurement.formShapedMeans: extension .pdf or .docx — the shapes an official form takes. Reference captures (.html) are excluded from this count and are counted in notHeldAtAnyHash.

whatThisDoesNotEstablish: That any particular unheld file serves any particular blocked family. The link measured here is jurisdictional, not per-obligation, so 99 is an UPPER BOUND on what mounting would unblock and not a forecast.
That any of these files is the current official edition. The inventory records what was collected, with an mtime; it does not establish currentness.
That any of them is the document a family names. Only opening one and reading its face establishes identity, and this comparison opened nothing.
theArkansasExceptionAndWhyItMisleads: FABLE-DISC05 measured Arkansas and found 22 of 26 Nationwide files byte-identical to the Master Library, concluding that for Arkansas a mount is cheaper than a fetch. That is correct for Arkansas and does not generalise: nationally only 212 of 583 are duplicates. Arkansas is the best-covered state in the inventory, not a representative one.
